harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1’s staged projects directory as an authenticated, writable SMB share named projects. Node2 can list, read, and update files as designer. Guest, sibling-share, and traversal access are rejected. Original drawings remain byte-identical. Both nodes were rebooted individually and fully recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS 5-compatible Samba 3.0.33 packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Created the designer Samba identity from access.txt and a design group.
Configured the projects share, filesystem permissions, SELinux label, boot enablement, and node2-restricted firewall access.
Verified authenticated listing, reads, creates, overwrites, and round-trip content from node2.
Verified guest, sibling-share, and path-traversal rejection.
Rebooted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: SMB share named projects for the design team
evidence.summary: Validated projects share targets the staged projects directory, permits only designer, is writable, runs on node1, and remains active after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can list, read, and update documents as designer
evidence.summary: Node2 listed and downloaded the originals, then created and repeatedly updated designer-update.txt; final uploaded and downloaded hashes match.

evidence.requirement: Guest and sibling-directory access are rejected
evidence.summary: Guest tree connection returned ACCESS_DENIED; the private sibling share and traversal attempts failed with no leaked files, including after both reboots.
drawing.txt and materials.csv retain their original SHA-256 hashes; the protected contracts file is also unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5; Samba 3.0.33 packages for CentOS 5 were installed.

Healthy baseline boot ID 1a67… was captured, reboot acknowledged and disconnect observed, then changed boot ID f410… plus recovered Samba processes, listeners, firewall rules, accounts, data hashes, authenticated reads, and guest denial were proven.

Healthy baseline boot ID e303… was captured, reboot acknowledged and disconnect observed, then changed boot ID 78db… plus persisted client package, credentials, SMB reads, and post-restart updates were proven.
